intro.title: useEffect & Side Effects
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a dynamic user profile component that automatically fetches and displays user data when the component loads, and updates the page title based on the selected user. You'll learn about side effects in Angular - operations that interact with the outside world like API calls, DOM manipulation, or timers - and how to manage them properly using lifecycle hooks. The main concepts covered include the ngOnInit lifecycle hook for component initialization, dependency injection for services, and proper cleanup with ngOnDestroy. You'll work with Angular's component lifecycle, HTTP client for data fetching, and reactive programming patterns using RxJS observables. By the end, you'll understand when and how to perform side effects in Angular components while avoiding common pitfalls like memory leaks.
intro.usecase: Side effects with useEffect are essential in modern web applications for handling data fetching, subscriptions, and cleanup operations. You'll find this pattern in e-commerce sites that fetch product data when components mount, social media feeds that subscribe to real-time updates, and dashboard applications that poll APIs for live metrics. Dating apps use useEffect to track user location changes, streaming platforms manage video player lifecycle events, and banking apps handle authentication token refreshes. Every time you see a loading spinner, auto-updating content, or real-time notifications in apps like Slack, Twitter, or Airbnb, useEffect is managing those side effects behind the scenes.
